score_100.reason: This rubric allocates most of the score to the core scientific result: the fraction of time that the scene-bump offset spent in the out-phase range increased significantly from the pre-learning epoch to the learning epoch and then decreased significantly from the learning epoch to the post-learning epoch. These epoch-dependent changes demonstrate that the symmetric scene most strongly disrupted landmark anchoring during the learning epoch. Statistical details such as signed-rank tests and the exact out-phase definition support the conclusion but are secondary to preserving the main across-epoch pattern and biological interpretation.

Scoring items.criterion: States the main epoch-dependent pattern that the fraction out-phase increased from pre-learning to learning and decreased from learning to post-learning
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 30 points if the across-epoch pattern is missing, substantially incomplete, or reversed. Deduct 15-20 points if only part of the pattern is stated, such as mentioning an increase in the learning epoch without describing the subsequent decrease.

Scoring items.criterion: Preserves the core interpretation that scene-bump alignment or landmark anchoring was most disrupted during the learning epoch due to the symmetric scene
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 20 points if the disruption interpretation is omitted or replaced with an incorrect interpretation. Deduct 8-12 points if the answer mentions only generic changes across epochs without indicating that disruption was strongest in the learning epoch.

Scoring items.criterion: Identifies that the plotted metric is the fraction of time spent in the out-phase range of the scene-bump offset
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 15 points if the metric is not identified and the answer gives only a vague statement about misalignment. Deduct 6-10 points if the answer refers generally to large offsets or misalignment without clearly indicating it is a fraction of time.

Scoring items.criterion: Indicates that the out-phase range corresponds to large scene-bump offsets (for example |scene-bump offset| > 3π/4) or an equivalent description of strongly misaligned states
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 15 points if the out-phase concept is omitted entirely. Deduct 5-8 points if the answer mentions out-of-phase periods or large offsets but does not convey the threshold or strong-misalignment meaning.

Scoring items.criterion: Mentions that the comparisons across epochs were supported by signed-rank tests or that the changes were statistically significant
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 10 points if the statistical significance framework is completely missing. Deduct 3-5 points if significance is mentioned but the signed-rank comparison is not specified.

Scoring items.criterion: Notes that the plot includes individual fish (dots) connected by grey lines for the same fish across epochs
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 10 points only if the answer claims the panel shows population averages without individual data or completely omits the paired structure when describing the visualization; minor omission incurs no deduction if the scientific pattern is preserved.

Acceptable deviations: Paraphrasing 'fraction of time spent in the out-phase range' as 'proportion of time with large scene-bump mismatch', 'fraction of time with strong misalignment', or 'fraction of large-offset periods' is acceptable if the meaning is preserved
Paraphrasing 'scene-bump alignment was disrupted' as 'landmark anchoring was weakened', 'misalignment increased', or 'alignment deteriorated' is acceptable
Referring to the learning epoch as the 'symmetric scene epoch' or 'double-sun epoch' is acceptable if the temporal ordering is preserved
Omitting the exact |scene-bump offset| > 3π/4 threshold is acceptable for partial credit if the answer clearly conveys time spent in a strongly misaligned state
Omitting exact P values is acceptable if the answer clearly states that the changes were significant
Omitting minor visualization details (such as exact dot or line style) is acceptable
rubric.Scoring instructions: Assign points based on whether the answer preserves the main scientific result rather than figure-display details. Full credit requires capturing the epoch-wise pattern of increase from pre-learning to learning and decrease from learning to post-learning, the interpretation that disruption was strongest during the learning epoch due to the symmetric scene, and the fact that the metric was the fraction of time spent in the out-phase range. Partial credit should be given when the answer preserves the main trend and interpretation but simplifies the metric definition, out-phase details, or statistical framework. Low scores should be assigned when the answer reduces the panel to a generic visual description (e.g., only mentioning dots and lines) or fails to preserve the core epoch-dependent disruption pattern.
